source: Hegazy (2024) Diversity of Thought Elicits Stronger Reasoning Capabilities in Multi-Agent Debate Frameworks
finding: Debate between three different model families beat debate between copies of one model on GSM8K.
numbers: Solo GSM8K accuracy: Gemini-Pro 78%, PaLM 2-M 64%, Mixtral 8x7B 70%. Diverse debate after 4 rounds: 91%. Three Gemini-Pro copies: 82% (80% without CoT).
limits: Small journal, single author, 4 rounds, 2023-24 models; no confidence intervals seen.
agent_relevance: Model diversity, not just agent count, is the lever. Different model families act like different standpoints.

source: Hegazy (2024) Diversity of Thought Elicits Stronger Reasoning Capabilities in Multi-Agent Debate Frameworks
finding: Diverse debate set a new best score on ASDiv and worked for small models too.
numbers: ASDiv: solo 89%, 86%, 81%; debate 94%. Small models: diverse debate gave +17% by round 4 versus +10% for the homogeneous group on GSM8K.
limits: Same caveats. The claim to beat GPT-4 compares against a reported GPT-4 number.
agent_relevance: Cheap heterogeneous ensembles can beat one strong model on closed-answer tasks.

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Multiagent debate (3 agents, 2 rounds) beat single agent, reflection and majority vote on math and chess.
numbers: Arithmetic: single 67.0, reflection 72.1, majority 69.0, debate 81.8. GSM8K: 77.0, 75.0, 81.0, 85.0. Chess pawn score: 91.4, 102.1, 102.2, 122.9.
limits: Same model copies; small samples (+-2 to 5 points). Later work found gains vanish against strong baselines.
agent_relevance: Founding result for society of minds. Debate is the LLM analogue of Longino's transformative criticism.

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Different persona prompts (professor, doctor, mathematician) lifted MMLU a little.
numbers: MMLU 71.1 to 74.2 with different persona initialisation.
limits: Small gain, one dataset, no variance given. Prompt-level diversity only.
agent_relevance: Persona diversity is weak but cheap; model diversity is stronger (see Hegazy).

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Agents drift to consensus; prompts that make agents stubborn lengthen debate and improve results.
numbers: Qualitative consensus plots across rounds; 20-problem GSM8K study.
limits: Convergence is the transient-diversity problem in miniature.
agent_relevance: Disagreement must be protected during the run or the group collapses early.

source: Liang et al. (2024) Encouraging Divergent Thinking in LLMs through Multi-Agent Debate
finding: Self-reflection suffers Degeneration-of-Thought: once confident, a model cannot produce new views even if wrong. Debate with opposing agents and a judge is the fix.
numbers: Abstract and intro read; disagreement-by-round plot shows disagreement falling toward 0 under reflection.
limits: Only abstract and intro read; tables not extracted.
agent_relevance: A single agent needs an explicit dissent step because it does not self-generate standpoints.

source: Smit et al. (2024) Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
finding: Failed replication of broad MAD superiority: debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling, but is very sensitive to hyperparameters.
numbers: Several MAD protocols on 6 datasets with GPT-4 and Mixtral 8x7B; Multi-Persona improved after tuning; modulating prompted initial agreement raised accuracy on USMLE and MedQA.
limits: Abstract and figure captions read; per-cell numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: The prompted level of disagreement matters; too much agreement kills the benefit.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate - We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
finding: 5 MAD methods on 9 benchmarks with 4 models mostly fail to beat Chain-of-Thought or Self-Consistency despite more compute.
numbers: Multi-Persona won 0% against CoT; ChatEval and AgentVerse beat CoT in about 15% of cases; only one MAD (Claude-3.5-haiku, MMLU) beat CoT, by +0.85%.
limits: Limited to chosen frameworks and prompts.
agent_relevance: Homogeneous debate is mostly costly waste; do not build on the 2023 claims alone.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate - We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
finding: Model heterogeneity is the fix: mixing GPT-4o-mini and Llama3.1-70b inside MAD consistently helped.
numbers: Heter-SoM beat SoM-average by 6.4%; Heter-EoT beat EoT-average by 8.2%; all Heter-MAD beat CoT-average by up to 5.8%. Model drawn at random p=0.5 per agent.
limits: Only two candidate models; gains smaller for ChatEval and AgentVerse.
agent_relevance: Supports the cognitive-diversity claim for machines: different training means a different standpoint.

source: Li et al. (2025) Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?
finding: Counter-result: sampling one strong model many times (Self-MoA) beat mixing different models.
numbers: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate: Self-MoA 65.7 vs mixed MoA 59.1 (+6.6). Average +3.8% over MMLU, CRUX, MATH. Best single Qwen1.5-110B-Chat 43.9; mixed WizardLM-2-8x22B 53.1.
limits: Holds when one model is clearly best; mixing helps when models are close in quality.
agent_relevance: Diversity is not free: mixing weak with strong lowers average quality. Boundary condition.

source: Li et al. (2025) Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?
finding: Quality-diversity trade-off quantified by regression.
numbers: MoA performance regressed on quality and Vendi-score diversity; both p<0.001; R2 about 0.7 on each of MMLU, CRUX, MATH; about 70 data points per dataset.
limits: Linear fit on normalised terms.
agent_relevance: Diversity pays only if member quality is kept up. Echoes Hong-Page limits.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
finding: Large-scale test: LLMs collapse to the same answers within and across models on open-ended prompts.
numbers: INFINITY-CHAT: 26K real open-ended queries; 70+ models; same-model pairwise embedding similarity typically above 0.8 (top-p 0.9, temp 1.0); across models 71% to 82% (DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82; vs gpt-4o 0.81).
limits: Embedding similarity is coarse; shared synthetic data is a suspected cause, not proven.
agent_relevance: Voting across different models gives less independence than assumed. Ensembles are partly one standpoint.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
finding: Decoding tweaks do not fix collapse.
numbers: Temp 2.0 with min-p 0.1: 79% of cases still above 0.8 similarity; min-p setting: 81% of pairs above 0.7 and 61.2% above 0.8.
limits: Aggressive sampling hurts coherence, so this is a best case.
agent_relevance: Temperature is not a substitute for real viewpoint diversity.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
finding: Models, reward models and LLM judges align poorly with humans where people disagree.
numbers: Human data: 25 raters per item; 18,750 absolute labels (50 prompts x 15 responses) and 12,500 pairwise labels. Correlation with 56 LM, reward-model and judge scorers drops on similar-quality and high-disagreement subsets.
limits: Single survey population.
agent_relevance: An LLM judge hides minority preference; keep dissent unfiltered.

source: Wang, Morgenstern, Dickerson (2025) Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups
finding: Direct test of standpoint claims: identity-prompted LLMs do not reproduce in-group views.
numbers: 3200 human participants, 16 identities, 4 LLMs, 9 questions. LLM answers closer to out-group imitation than in-group portrayal for non-binary (16/24; 32/48) and impaired vision (18/24; 27/48); Gen Z 27/48; woman 26/48.
limits: Subjective-opinion questions showed little effect. Runs July-Aug 2023.
agent_relevance: Persona prompts do not carry lived standpoint. Do not use a role label as a stand-in for outside perspectives.

source: Wang, Morgenstern, Dickerson (2025) Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups
finding: Flattening: LLM answers vary less than human group answers, and temperature does not fix it.
numbers: SBERT covariance lower for LLMs; GPT-4 tested at temperatures 1.0, 1.2, 1.4; only at 1.4 (near-nonsense text) did unique n-grams match humans; other three diversity measures stayed below human.
limits: Authors also note identity prompts can essentialise groups.
agent_relevance: Sampling many personas from one model does not imitate a real community.

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Towards an AI co-scientist
finding: Multi-agent generate-debate-evolve system with Elo tournament: an adversarial structure built into a discovery agent.
numbers: Self-play debate and Elo ranking over 203 research goals; Elo concordant with GPQA-diamond accuracy; top-ranked answer reaches 78.4% top-1 on GPQA diamond; Elo kept rising with test-time compute, no saturation seen.
limits: Elo is self-judged; expert evaluation on 15 goals (11 in preference study). AML and cf-PICIs are case studies.
agent_relevance: Closest deployed instance of Longino-style critical interaction in an LLM loop (debate, ranking, meta-review).

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Towards an AI co-scientist
finding: Ablation numbers: refinement and review agents give modest gains.
numbers: Improvement step: GPQA precision 70.9% to 75.4%. Meta-review agent AUC 0.629 to 0.634 on GPQA (1680 ideas) and 0.521 to 0.597 on paper-QA (600 ideas); correlation with quality 0.101 to 0.226.
limits: Gains small on GPQA; no human-diverse-team control arm.
agent_relevance: Specialised roles each add a little; no single strategy dominated.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review: LLM ideas rated more novel than human expert ideas.
numbers: Novelty human 4.84, AI 5.64, AI plus human rerank 5.81 (49 ideas each; 298 reviews; 100+ researchers); p<0.05 for novelty; feasibility slightly lower.
limits: Idea-level, not outcome-level. Reviews subjective.
agent_relevance: Shows LLM novelty; next row shows its diversity limit.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: LLM idea generation lacks diversity: scaling by sampling saturates.
numbers: Of 4000 generated seed ideas only about 200 were non-duplicates (cosine cutoff 0.8); non-duplicate share per batch keeps falling; accumulation plateaus.
limits: NLP topics only.
agent_relevance: Repeated sampling of one model is not a population of researchers; force diversity.

source: Measuring epistemic diversity of LLMs across time and cultures (2025)
finding: First large measure of epistemic diversity (diversity of real-world claims) in LLM outputs.
numbers: 27 LLMs, 155 topics, 12 countries, 1.7M responses, 70M claims. Diversity rose over 3 years, yet every model stayed below a search baseline; larger models less diverse than smaller; RAG raised diversity.
limits: Claim extraction uses an NLI model; English bias on country topics.
agent_relevance: Retrieval from varied sources adds claim diversity; supports an outside-evidence step over more samples.

source: Peterson (2025) AI and the Problem of Knowledge Collapse
finding: Formal model: if learners favour cheap AI output, public belief drifts from truth and the tails of knowledge vanish.
numbers: Default model: a 20% discount on AI-generated content gave public beliefs 2.3 times further from truth than no discount.
limits: Stylised simulation; abstract and intro read.
agent_relevance: A single agent fed on its own outputs narrows; keep outside sources.

source: Fazelpour, O'Brien, Rubin (2026) Navigating Epistemic Monocultures in AI-Driven Science: A Simulation Study
finding: NK-landscape agent model (descendant of Weisberg-Muldoon) of scientists with AI advisors: uniform AI guidance helps only under narrow conditions, otherwise premature convergence.
numbers: Over 1000 runs with 100 agents, communities converged to one solution (mean pairwise Hamming distance near 0). Benefit only for decomposable problems and moderate AI use.
limits: Simulation, not LLM agents.
agent_relevance: Uniform advice from one model homogenises; the lesson applies to ensembles from one base model.

source: Fazelpour, O'Brien, Rubin (2026) Navigating Epistemic Monocultures in AI-Driven Science: A Simulation Study
finding: Mitigations: randomisation (sampling among top answers) helps only on decomposable problems; personalisation helps across a broad range.
numbers: Personalised AI beat non-personalised and randomised at varied use rates and problem types (qualitative, from abstract and intro).
limits: Benefits need institutional norms.
agent_relevance: Random variety is weaker than context-tailored diversity.

source: Weisberg and Muldoon (2009) Epistemic Landscapes and the Division of Cognitive Labor
finding: Agent model: mixed populations of followers and mavericks explore a landscape better than pure ones; mavericks stimulate followers.
numbers: Snippet only; no figures read.
limits: Not opened. Critiques: small rule changes alter results.
agent_relevance: Prior art for any simulated division of labor among agents.

source: Poyhonen (2017) Modelling the division of cognitive labour and heterogeneity of learning heuristics
finding: Extension: social learning and cognitive diversity help only when problems are hard enough.
numbers: Snippet only.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Diversity is a tool for hard problems, not every task.

source: Longino (1990) Science as Social Knowledge; (2002) The Fate of Knowledge
finding: Objectivity comes from transformative criticism among diverse perspectives, with four norms: venues, uptake, shared standards, tempered equality.
numbers: None (philosophy).
limits: Not opened; from prior knowledge.
agent_relevance: Norms map to debate design: venues (rounds), uptake (answer the critic), shared standards (rubric), equal voice (no judge bias).

source: Hong and Page (2004) Groups of diverse problem solvers can outperform groups of high-ability problem solvers
finding: Original diversity-trumps-ability result; later critiqued as mathematically fragile.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened. The MoA quality-diversity regression (c11-c12) is the machine-side version.
agent_relevance: Measure quality and diversity, not diversity alone.
